purpose: This medication is used to treat ear infections, specifically infections of the middle ear in children with ear tubes, or infections of the outer ear canal (sometimes called swimmer's ear) in both adults and children. It helps clear up the infection while also reducing pain, swelling, and irritation inside the ear. Your doctor prescribed it to help you feel better faster by tackling both the infection and the inflammation at the same time.
how_it_works: Ciprofloxacin is an antibiotic that kills the bacteria causing your ear infection by stopping the bacteria from being able to grow and reproduce. Dexamethasone is a steroid that calms down the swelling, redness, and discomfort in your ear. Together, they make a powerful team — one fights the infection while the other soothes the irritation.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are mild and happen right in the ear, such as a temporary stinging, burning, or itching sensation when you put the drops in. Some people notice a slight discomfort or a feeling of fullness in the ear. These effects are usually short-lived and not a reason to stop using the drops.
warnings: Do not use these drops in your eyes — they are for ears only. Do not use them if your eardrum has a hole or is ruptured, unless your doctor specifically told you it is safe to do so. If you notice a rash, severe itching, or your symptoms get worse instead of better, contact your doctor right away. Keep this medication away from children's reach and do not share it with others.
typical_dosing: For most adults and children, the usual dose is 4 drops placed into the affected ear(s) twice a day for 7 days. Before using, warm the bottle in your hands for a minute or two — this helps prevent dizziness from cold drops. Lie on your side, put the drops in, and stay lying down for about a minute so the drops can settle in. Always finish the full course even if you start feeling better early.
